tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter × height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft. Add wall_height_ft field; wall paint SF/room = perimeter × height. Emit a 'Wall paint area' line per room.

prep.what: Compute wall square footage from room perimeter × height so painting jobs get real measurements instead of zero.
prep.understand: The engine gives 2D geometry — room polygons with perimeter in feet. Painting is priced on wall area (height × perimeter) not floor area. TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php currently drops geometry entirely, so painting gets $0 lines. Need wall_height_ft on estimates (project-level default) and the seeder must read perimeter from geometry.
approach: Add `wall_height_ft` nullable decimal column to `estimates` via migration (default 9.0 ft).
Expose wall height input in estimate edit UI (Estimates/Edit.vue or seeder input surface).
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, stop dropping geometry — read `meta.perimeter` per room and compute `wall_sf = perimeter × wall_height_ft`.
Emit a `kind='painting'` estimate line per room with derived wall_sf.

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: Add PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft' to RateType enum; wire LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType->'lf'; seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before takeoff pricing.

prep.what: Add a per-linear-foot rate type to the estimate system so trim and wall-linear measurements can be priced correctly.
prep.understand: RateType is a PHP enum used by LineItemFactory to determine unit labels. PerLinearFt must be added before any takeoff measurement can be priced by LF. This is a prerequisite (t48 depends on it).
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to `app/Enums/RateType.php` with a display label.
Update `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` to return `'lf'` for PerLinearFt.
Add a trim LaborRate row in `database/seeders/LaborRateSeeder.php`.
Run the seeder in dev and verify the option appears in the estimate editor.

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into anonymous kind=custom $0 line. Preserve+switch on kind: area(SF)->flooring, derived wall SF->painting, line(LF)->wall-linear/trim, count(EA)->doors/tile.

prep.what: Split takeoff measurements by trade type (flooring/painting/trim/doors) instead of dumping everything as a single unlabeled custom line.
prep.understand: Seeder ignores the measurement `kind` field from engine (area/line/count) and emits one generic kind=custom line. Rafa needs separate trade lines. `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` helper defines painting/flooring as self-performed vs subcontracted.
approach: In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, read the `kind` field on each measurement from engine response.
Switch on kind: `area` → flooring, derived wall SF → painting (t45), `line` → trim using PerLinearFt (t47), `count` → door/tile line.
Tag each line with trade using `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` to set `is_subcontracted`.
Run test takeoff through seeder and verify each type gets its own labeled line.
resources: t45 and t47 must be done first

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Rooms show 'unnamed' for outlined-text firms (PDFTron outlines ALL text). v2: (a) productize M3 tiles lane as opt-in 'read labels (AI)'; (b) callout-vs-room filtering.

prep.what: Build the AI-powered label reading lane for firms where PDFTron outlines all text (zero readable chars in free lane).
prep.understand: Live-text lane reads raw PDF characters. CAD-outlined text firms (Harborview demo) produce zero characters → rooms show 'unnamed'. M3 tiles spike (run_labels_m3tiles.py) proved the fix works at ~4.3 min/sheet via MiniMax vision. Second half: filtering noise — Holabird free-text lane picks up stair arrows, FEC notes, paragraphs as fake room names.
approach: Productize `run_labels_m3tiles.py` as an opt-in service route (e.g. `POST /sheets/{id}/read-labels?mode=vision`) — this is the metered-credits path.
Wire MINIMAX_AI key as a required secret for this route (similar to API_KEYS_RAW).
Build callout-vs-room filter: remove strings matching non-room patterns (all-caps direction words like 'UP', FEC/EXIT/STAIR annotations, strings > N words suggesting paragraphs).
Test Harborview through M3 lane (confirm labels); test Holabird through filter (confirm paragraph callouts excluded).
resources: `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` — proven M3 vision spike to productize
Holabird sheet as the noise filtering test case (R13 documented)

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: PRD Phase 1. Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). Last pillar between us and estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Expand the assemblies system so each classified room type produces multiple quantity outputs (paint SF, drywall SF, flooring SF, wall heights) from a single room polygon.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` scaffolding exists (assemblies-lite shipped in B1). Full version needs room-type → assembly formula library: a painting room gets wall paint SF (perimeter × height), ceiling SF (floor area), flooring SF, etc. CSI division codes organize types. Wall height is the key input not in 2D geometry — must be set per-project or per-room-type.
approach: Define room-type → assembly map in `engine/assemblies.py`: classification → list of (surface, formula, CSI code). Start with painting/flooring/drywall for most common types.
Build wall height registry: project-level default with room-type overrides (e.g. 9ft residential, 12ft commercial corridor).
For each room, compute each assembly quantity using `geometry.rings` (perimeter, area) + height registry.
Output per-room quantity rows in existing SheetData format so Excel lane picks them up via `build_sheet_takeoff`.
resources: CSI MasterFormat Division 09 (Finishes) — standard assembly codes
`STATE.md` Phase 1 assembly notes — prior design decisions
